title: Support for a child with autism (ABA therapy)
what: These are sessions where a child is taught new skills step by step: communicating, playing, taking care of themselves. The child is praised and rewarded for each success.
why: For children with autism spectrum disorder, especially at an early age.
duration: sessions usually take a few hours a week; the course lasts months to years
tell_doctor: What your child can do now and what worries you
What your child likes: toys, food, activities, since these are used as rewards

prepare.title: List
prepare.text: Write down your child's favorite toys and treats. They will be needed in sessions.

prepare.title: Routine
prepare.text: Plan sessions for when your child is rested and has eaten.

prepare.title: Getting ready
prepare.text: If a new place is hard for your child, show them a photo of the room or the specialist beforehand.

steps: The specialist meets your child and watches them
Assesses which skills are there and which are missing
In sessions, teaches skills in small steps
Rewards your child for each success
Teaches you to practice the skills at home
feel: At first it may be hard and unfamiliar for your child
There may be protests and tears, and the specialist knows how to work with that
after: Practice the skills at home using the specialist's advice
Note what has changed and tell the specialist at sessions
Take care of yourself too, since parents also need rest and support
red_flags: If your child hurts themselves or others, talk to your doctor and the specialist
A sudden loss of skills they already had: see a doctor

faq.q: How many hours a week are needed?
faq.a: It varies, and it is often many hours. The specialist will set the load to fit your child.
Autism does not go away. But sessions help a child become more independent and communicate more easily.

reminders.text: Your child's session is today. Bring favorite toys, treats, and a change of clothes.
